Meteor showers 2026–2027

ZHR is the number of meteors per hour that an observer would see under a perfectly dark sky with the radiant high above the horizon; in cities and in moonlight far fewer are visible. The Moon's illumination is at the moment of the peak.

Eclipses visible from Bulgaria

Partial solar eclipse – 2 August 2027

Visible from all of Bulgaria. In Sofia the eclipse begins at 11:18, the maximum is at 12:25 (about 53% of the Sun's disk is covered, magnitude 0.67) and it ends at 13:41. It is total in a band that passes over Gibraltar and North Africa. Never look at the Sun without special eclipse glasses. Source: time.now – eclipses in Sofia (calculated data).

The eclipses of 12 and 28 August 2026 have already passed (the solar one was visible only in the north-westernmost parts of Bulgaria, and the lunar one only at the start, low in the west).

Supermoons 2026–2027

A supermoon is a full moon when the Moon is close to its perigee. There is no exact definition: according to NASA, quoted by Space.com, it is a full moon at a distance of less than about 362,000 km. The dates and times of the full moons are calculated by our Moon calendar, and the "supermoon" label comes from the cited source. The difference in apparent size is small.

Northern lights in Bulgaria

Loading Kp…

The northern lights are seen from Bulgaria very rarely. Kp is a measure of geomagnetic activity from 0 to 9. The usual "magnetic storms" (Kp 5–6) light up the sky only north of Europe. To see an aurora from our latitudes, Kp usually has to be around 7 or more (levels G3 and above on the NOAA scale), with a clear sky, far from city lights and looking north.

It happens only with the strongest storms. For example, in the early hours of 11 October 2024 the aurora was visible from Bulgaria too (BTA). So most of the "storms" in the news do not mean an aurora over us.
